text:
Marathon Petroleum edged up 0.24% today to $478.07, barely moving in what has otherwise been a volatile two-week stretch. The stock is up 13.2% over that span, driven mostly by sharp oil price swings—Brent crude jumped to $110 this week as Iran escalated attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint for global oil supply. With U.S. refineries running at 93.5% capacity and crude prices near $102, refiners benefit from the wider gap between what they pay for oil and what they can sell refined products for.

The bigger picture is geopolitical risk pushing oil higher across the board. Tanker rates have also surged, adding real physical costs to moving oil globally—one analyst noted that transportation alone can add ~$38 per barrel to the actual cost of delivery. This combination of tight refinery utilization, elevated crude prices, and supply-chain stress from regional conflict creates a favorable environment for U.S. refining margins, which explains the stock's strong run over the past two weeks even as today's action stayed flat.
